   - `publication_year`: 4-digit year printed on the paper/report itself (e.g. `"2024"`), or `"not reported"` if undated. Give exact page/header in `where_found`.
   - `country`: Country or countries studied as stated in the paper (use semicolon-separated names if multiple specific countries, or exact global/regional scope as stated, e.g. `"Global (48 countries)"`), or `"not reported"`.
   - `sample_size`: Exact sample size(s) AND explicit unit(s) of analysis stated in the paper (e.g. `"593 households across 4 neighbourhoods"`, `"128 municipalities; 2,048 observations (2010-2025)"`, `"32 semi-structured interviews"`), or `"not reported"` if pure doctrinal/legal analysis with no empirical sample.
   - `study_design`: Study design as the authors describe it and as operationalized in the methods section (be specific about quantitative/qualitative/quasi-experimental/experimental/review structure).
   - `effect_estimate`: Headline result of the study regarding how the legal, administrative, regulatory, institutional, tenure, tariff/subsidy, or participation factor relates to water/sanitation access/outcomes, with exact printed numbers (point estimates, units, 95% CIs, p-values, sample N) if quantitative, or concise factual headline finding if qualitative (noting `"Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported"` when purely qualitative), in your own words from the paper alone.
   - `risk_of_bias_tool`: Pick the single design-matched tool per `RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1:
     * `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"` (individually randomized trial)
     * `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"` (cluster-randomized trial — check unit of randomization carefully!)
     * `"ROBINS-I"` (non-randomized intervention / quasi-experimental study with a genuine comparator: DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, policy panel FE)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"` (quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without quasi-experimental intervention comparator)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"` (observational longitudinal cohort study without intervention framing)
     * `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"` (primary qualitative study: interviews, focus groups, ethnography, qualitative case study)
     * `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"` (genuine mixed-methods study combining both qualitative and quantitative primary components)
     * `"AMSTAR 2"` (systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with systematic search/screening; NEVER use for non-systematic narrative literature reviews)
     * `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"` (legal-empirical, doctrinal-empirical, jurimetric, or institutional-historical study that fits none of the six conventional designs above)
     * `"NONE"` (fits none of the listed tools, e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model, or non-systematic narrative review/essay without primary empirical data or systematic search — explain why in `comment`)
   - `mechanism_certainty`: Single integer `"0"`, `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, or `"4"` strictly obeying `CODEBOOK.md` §9 and its design ceiling:
     * `"4"` ONLY for randomized trials (`RoB 2`)
     * `"3"` ONLY for `RoB 2` trials OR `ROBINS-I` studies with credible Low/Moderate overall risk of bias
     * All other designs (cross-sectional/JBI, cohort, qualitative/CASP, mixed-methods/MMAT, systematic review/AMSTAR 2, Legal Framework, NONE, or Serious/Critical ROBINS-I) CANNOT exceed `"2"`! (`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).

   - `mechanism_flags`: Comma-separated list of applicable top-level family codes (`ELIGIBILITY`, `BURDEN`, `DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION`, `ENFORCEMENT`) followed by exact detailed `CODEBOOK.md` §4 codes actually studied in the paper (`documentation`, `tenure`, `property`, `planning`, `zoning`, `building_permit`, `service_area`, `fees`, `procedural_steps`, `delay`, `discretion`, `hardship_exception`, `accommodation`, `administrative_review`, `complaint`, `judicial_review`, `disconnection`, `reconnection`, `sanction`, `participation`, `institutional_fragmentation`, `political_coordination`, `bureaucratic_assistance`), or `"not reported"`.

country.comment: Trial conducted in rural villages across four provinces of the Democratic Republic of Congo: Kongo Central, Kasai, Kasai Central, and South Kivu (North Kivu was excluded prior to randomisation due to having only three clusters).
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF p. 2, Introduction; PDF p. 3, Methods (Study design and participants)

effect_estimate.comment: Primary and secondary outcomes were self-reported and analysed via linear intention-to-treat models with strata fixed effects and cluster-robust SEs. Text rounds secondary index effects to 1 decimal place (eg, 1.3 SDs for water governance, 0.6 SD for water satisfaction); Table 3 prints exact 2-decimal estimates. Subgroup effects varied significantly by province and remoteness (Tables 4-5).
effect_estimate.value: Intention-to-treat linear models (N = 1,312 households across 121 clusters, median 5 months post-intervention) found the VEA community-driven WASH and governance programme increased access to an improved primary water source by 33 percentage points (ITT 0.33, 95% CI 0.22 to 0.45; 83% intervention vs 43% control) and improved primary sanitation facility by 26 percentage points (ITT 0.26, 95% CI 0.14 to 0.37; 46% vs 18%), with no statistically significant overall effect on time spent collecting water (-3.0 min, 95% CI -19.7 to 13.6) or water quantity collected (+2.3 L, 95% CI -4.2 to 8.7). Among secondary outcomes, VEA increased the village-level water governance index (N = 328 villages) by 1.33 SD (95% CI 1.12 to 1.54), household water satisfaction index by 0.64 SD (95% CI 0.43 to 0.85), handwashing practices index by 0.48 SD (95% CI 0.25 to 0.71), and sanitation practices index by 0.28 SD (95% CI 0.12 to 0.44), with no significant effect on the financial cost of water index (+0.13 SD, 95% CI -0.10 to 0.36) or village-level water quality and access index (+0.13 SD, 95% CI -0.18 to 0.44).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 6-7, Results (Primary outcomes; Secondary outcomes), Table 2, and Table 3

mechanism_certainty.comment: Pre-registered cluster-randomised controlled trial (AEARCTR-0004648) appraised with RoB 2 that experimentally assigned the community-driven VEA programme and directly measured impacts on village water governance (+1.33 SD) and improved water/sanitation access (+33 pp / +26 pp). Note that VEA bundles participatory governance, Health Zone bureaucratic support, and Healthy Village certification with village infrastructure grants (approx. US$4,000/village for water and sanitation infrastructure), so the governance mechanism is not experimentally isolated from infrastructure financing, and outcomes are self-reported by unblinded respondents.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 3-5, Methods; PDF p. 6-7, Results, Tables 2-3; PDF p. 9, Discussion

mechanism_flags.comment: VEA operates through community-driven participation (collective community decision to request entry, participatory action planning, election and gender composition of a village WASH committee), bureaucratic assistance from Health Zone and Health Area officials (3-6 months of NGO/government support, volunteer training, monthly/weekly supervisory visits, co-developed maintenance plans), a 9-step administrative protocol (formal request, signed Health Zone agreement, baseline/follow-up evaluations, Chief Medical Officer inspection and Healthy Village certification), and village water user payments/financing (financial cost of water index and petty cash management training).

outcome_flags.comment: Primary outcomes measured household use of an improved drinking water source and collection time (water_access), household use of an improved sanitation facility (sanitation_access), and litres of water collected per day (service_quantity). Secondary outcomes measured household payment for water via the financial cost of water index (affordability) and the village-level water quality and access / functional improved water points index (service_quality), alongside water governance and water satisfaction indices.
